page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with hyperthreading. The processor is configured with 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with AES cryptographic acceleration.

The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU typical of compute-focused platforms. It does not include hardware GPUs and offers no local instance storage, requiring all persistent and non-volatile data to be handled over attached network block storage. Networking capability is configured with a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth, though the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. Single-core performance falls in the lower tiers, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1017.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1103.28, which translates to slower per-thread execution in tasks such as single-threaded gzip compression (19.17 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded execution benefits significantly from the 64 virtual cores, reaching an average Geekbench multi-core score of 10572.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 38269.32. Memory throughput registers at 118.53 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 38.35 GB/sec for writes.

Given its hardware density, the ecs.c5.16xlarge presents a compute-dense profile well-suited for highly concurrent and scale-out workloads that do not demand cutting-edge single-thread latency. Relevant workload fits include multi-threaded batch processing, Clang software builds, distributed container hosting, microservices architectures, and parallelized backend web serving where aggregate core count compensates for individual thread speed.

Reflecting a strict 1:2 memory-to-CPU ratio, it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for remote resources. Benchmark evaluations reveal weaker single-thread metrics, such as a single-core Geekbench score of 1017.0 and single-thread gzip speeds of 19.17 GB/sec, contrasted by robust multi-threaded parallel execution across its 64 vCPUs (10572.0 Geekbench multi-core and 47219.61 stress-ng multi-core). This resource profile offers cost-effective parallel throughput, making it suitable for distributed microservices, multi-threaded batch jobs, software compilation, and scalable web serving workloads.
